Alex — great to meet today, thanks for sending the MAP draft. High-level: we can meet the target close date if we run the technical evaluation as the top priority. I sketched a proposed technical evaluation milestone below (also attached as an editable spreadsheet: acme-tech-eval-specs.xlsx).

Proposed MAP milestone: Technical evaluation plan (owner: Redwood engineering + Acme infra)
- Scope: end-to-end quality, latency/cost, and reliability testing on a representative Acme traffic sample (10k example queries across mapping, routing, and POI summarization).
- Success criteria (pass/fail thresholds):
  - Quality: match-or-exceed baseline model for key intents (mapping QA set) with >=95% intent accuracy on the eval set and no >3% regression on critical intents.
  - Latency: p50 <= 120 ms, p95 <= 420 ms for tail-sensitive routes under our expected concurrency profile.
  - Cost: inference cost at or below $1.50 per 1k tokens (ballpark) for the shortlisted quantized model configurations.
- Deliverables:
  - Benchmark report (latency distribution, cost estimates, quality metrics)
  - Model shortlist with recommended quantization and serving profile
  - Recommended production config (batching, cache TTLs, routing policies)
- Timeline: kickoff 2027-04-04, benchmarking complete by 2027-05-15, decision expected by 2027-05-20.

Next steps:
1) Dev/infra access: Alex — can your infra team provide a sanitized sample of 10k user queries and a short list of representative endpoints by 2027-03-31?
2) Redwood will provision a dedicated eval environment (estimated 2-3 GPUs) and share credentials by 2027-04-04.
3) We'll run a small pilot (2 days) to validate test harness then full runs (7-10 days).

I've included Marissa and Dev to fill in technical specifics below. If that timeline works, I'll update the MAP doc and send a formal kickoff invite.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Adding technical details for the eval plan / benchmark spec. Quoting Camila's timeline below.

On Sat, Mar 27, 2027 at 6:12 PM Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Proposed MAP milestone: Technical evaluation plan (owner: Redwood engineering + Acme infra)
> - Scope: end-to-end quality, latency/cost, and reliability testing on a representative Acme traffic sample (10k example queries across mapping, routing, and POI summarization).

Technical notes / checklist (owner tags included):
- Test harness (Redwood / dev_patel): we will run both peak and steady-state profiles. Include warm-started KV cache runs to measure production-like latency.
- Model shortlist (internal recommendation):
  1) Llama-3-Stream-Chat (quantized int8) — strong instruction-following, tested in retrieval scenarios.
  2) Mistral-Instruct-Base (8-bit quantized) — favorable cost/latency tradeoff, good for short-form summarization.
  3) Falcon-40B-Instruct (8-bit quantized) — robust open-weight baseline for routing/POI tasks.
  4) RedPajama-INCITE-70B (4-bit quantized for eval) — quality ceiling candidate; expect higher cost and GPU memory needs.

- Success criteria (concrete):
  - Quality: intent accuracy >= 0.95 on the labeled QA set; mean ROUGE-L improvement >= 0.02 vs current baseline for summarization tasks.
  - Latency: p50 <= 110 ms, p95 <= 400 ms on the chosen load profile; cold-start token overhead < 30 ms.
  - Cost: target <= $1.25 per 1k tokens for production-like quantized configs; accept up to $2.50 per 1k tokens for the highest-quality candidate during eval (cost vs quality tradeoff).

- Benchmark procedure:
  1) Run warm-up (24 hrs continuous low qps) to populate caches.
  2) Execute 3 full experiment runs per model (steady-state and burst scenarios).
  3) Capture: latency histograms, GPU utilization, tokens/sec, KV hit rate, and per-query quality labels.
  4) Produce side-by-side report with recommended production profile and estimated monthly cost for 1M tokens.

Dependencies / blockers:
- Acme: provide sanitized query sample and labels by 2027-03-31. (owner: Acme infra)
- Network: SSO and access to VPC/endpoint for private eval if required (owner: Acme security)
- Redwood: allocate dedicated eval capacity and share runbook (owner: dev_patel)

I'll prepare the benchmark harness and a short runbook this week and share a run link. If the shortlist needs adjusting (e.g., you prefer any proprietary model or marketplace variant), let me know.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
